message.content: {"caption":"Two side-by-side system-instruction panels show how to extract generalizable memory items from successful and failed web-navigation trajectories.","description":"A two-column text figure has a gray “System Instruction” header above each panel and a gray “Input Prompt” bar near the bottom. The left panel concerns a trajectory in which an agent successfully completed a web-navigation task; the phrase identifying successful completion is highlighted green. Its guidelines ask for useful, generalizable memory items based on the successful trajectory. Notes say to first consider why the trajectory succeeded, then summarize insights; extract at most three items, avoid repetition, and focus on transferable insights rather than specific websites, queries, or strings. The shared Markdown output template contains a memory-item number, title, one-sentence description, and one-to-three sentences of content about insights for accomplishing the task. Under “Input Prompt,” the fields are “Query: <user query>” and “Trajectory: <trajectory that completes the query>.” The right panel concerns a trajectory in which the agent attempted the task but failed; the failed-outcome phrase is highlighted red. Its guidelines request helpful, generalizable memory items based on the failed trajectory. Notes say to first reflect on why it failed and summarize lessons or strategies to prevent failure, then apply the same limit of three items, avoid repetition, and focus on transferable insights rather than specific sites, queries, or strings. It uses the same Markdown memory-item template and has the same Query field; its Trajectory field reads “<trajectory that completes the query>.” The panels are parallel text instructions, with no arrows, connections, checks, or crosses.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
